Summary with FSR lens:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent and kept IORB at 4.4 percent, signaling still-restrictive policy amid “somewhat elevated” inflation and solid labor conditions.
- Key balance‑sheet change: “Beginning in April, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $25 billion to $5 billion.” This is a marginal easing versus prior QT pace.
- FSR-informed context: The Financial Stability Report highlights elevated vulnerabilities that temper risk sentiment:
  • Credit: CRE stress persists (rising CMBS delinquencies) and private credit growth raises business leverage; corporate bond defaults have edged up. SLOOS indicates credit remains tight for many borrowers.  
  • Market structure/liquidity: MMFs are very large (about $6.25T) and run-prone; reliance on short-term wholesale funding remains a monitoring point; standing repo/RRP facilities help, but tail risks persist.  
  • Interest-rate and duration risk: Banks’ HTM exposures and sensitivity to long rates remain watchpoints, even with system resilience and strong capital/liquidity.  
  • Macro-financial risks: Geopolitical tensions and U.S. fiscal sustainability are monitored; inflation pressures pose stability risks.  
- Interpretation: Slower QT is a modestly dovish tilt supportive of risk assets, but the FSR’s elevated (though manageable) vulnerabilities and the statement’s heightened uncertainty argue for caution. Waller’s dissent for continuing the faster runoff underscores internal debate and limits the dovish read.

Net take: Mildly positive, but less so than a pure policy read would suggest.
